Two years ago, Sonos expanded from wireless speakers into the over-ear headphone market. Sonos now appears to be preparing to launch a more premium successor model, incorporating artificial intelligence features.

Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are set to debut

Chris Welch reports for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, a premium successor to its 2024 Ace headphones.

An application filing discovered on Monday and submitted to the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) revealed the product name and showed up to five colour options, a more diverse palette than the original black and white offerings.

Sonos plans to hold a product launch event in September, and the timing of this filing suggests the Ace Ultra is likely to make its first appearance at that event.

The filing also contains technical clues, indicating the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Conrad acknowledged that the original headphones lacked sufficient whole-home integration features when launched, failing to stand out in the highly competitive market.

This time, Sonos appears to be tying its hardware more directly to a broader artificial intelligence strategy.

Conrad described the company's opportunity as conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home environment, operating across rooms through Sonos hardware and understanding the living habits of household members.

The company has extended its Sonos Voice Control to operate smart home systems such as Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March this year, equipped with an H2 chip, enhanced noise cancellation, and live translation. Siri artificial intelligence will also extend to AirPods via iOS 27.
